To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the taxonomy can be used to define a loss function that penalizes errors more heavily for classes that are closer in the taxonomy; 2) the taxonomy can also be used to define an SVM kernel function that exploits the similarity between classes; 3) the taxonomy can even be used to define class attributes that are used as features in the SVM; and 4) all three approaches can improve classification accuracy.

(i) the taxonomy of word senses can be exploited in word sense disambiguation, (ii) a hierarchical taxonomy of document categories can be used to improve the performance of text categorization, and (iii) a kernel defined over the set classes can be used to exploit the taxonomy in text categorization.

1) incorporating taxonomic information into the learning process can significantly improve the classification accuracy and 2) the relative position of the classes in the taxonomy is a key factor for the success of the approach.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of incorporating prior knowledge into the learning process and with the problem of how to specify meaningful loss functions.
learning from text using prior knowledge about the semantic relations between classes.
the development and application of machine learning techniques that exploit prior knowledge about the structure of the data.

we can learn classifiers from training data that are labeled with classes from an existing taxonomy and that we can learn from the same data a new taxonomy that is more suitable for classification.

the use of taxonomic knowledge in learning improves the performance of the classifiers.
